LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 3.3.1 CORRELATIVE CONJUNCTIONS

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.3: Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Correlative Conjunctions

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Correlative Conjunctions
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: Which words do we use when making a choice between two things?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. identify correlative conjunctions in an oral or written text
2. use correlative conjunctions correctly in oral and written communication
3. use the pattern show... nominal... how/where/who in sentences

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Correlative Conjunctions

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Correlative Conjunctions

Teach
• Focus skill: identify correlative conjunctions in an oral or written text.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Correlative Conjunctions.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Correlative Conjunctions
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Which words do we use when making a choice between two things?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
